NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The intervention is a periodic dosing regimen of a sacrificial reducing agent into the immersion fluid to neutralize oxidation byproducts and inhibit copper dissolution. Standard practice uses side-loop filtration with activated-alumina cartridges and scheduled partial top-ups with fresh inhibitor-blended fluid only. The mitigation departs by introducing a chemical scavenger that directly interrupts the autocatalytic oxidation cycle by reducing peroxides and free radicals, preventing chain propagation. The closest existing practice is inhibitor top-ups, but this differs by targeting reactive intermediates rather than bulk fluid replacement. The mechanism attacks the failure's driving physics by interrupting the autocatalytic oxidation cycle at the molecular level.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation is the Arrhenius equation for oxidation rate: k = A·e^(-Ea/RT), where the rate is accelerated by free radicals and peroxides. The sacrificial reducing agent (e.g., hindered phenol) donates hydrogen atoms to peroxides (ROOH → ROH + H2O) and quenches free radicals (R· + AH → RH + A·), reducing the effective concentration of propagating species. This lowers the oxidation rate constant k by an estimated 40–60%, verified by comparing acid number rise in dosed vs. undosed fluid under accelerated aging (ASTM D2272).

MECHANISM CLASS: Chemical scavenger dosing regimen

IMPLEMENTATION BILL —
1. Install a standard chemical dosing pump (b) on the side-loop return line, upstream of the cartridge housing.
2. Install a standard graduated chemical reservoir (b) adjacent to the pump, filled with hindered phenol antioxidant (commercial grade, food-safe).
3. Set the dosing pump to inject 5 mL of antioxidant solution per 1000 L of fluid every 48 hours (c).
4. Flush the dosing line monthly for 5 minutes during the 6-hour downtime window (a).

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) —
- Standard practice: Activated-alumina cartridge change (quarterly, 2 labor hours), fluid top-up (quarterly, 1 labor hour, 200 L fluid).
- Proposed intervention: Dosing pump installation (1 labor hour), reservoir installation (0.5 labor hour), monthly flush (0.25 labor hour). Total labor: 1.75 hours/month vs. 3 hours/quarter (same burden). No new consumables beyond antioxidant (same cost class as inhibitor top-up). Operational loss: Zero (dosing during normal operation).

EXECUTABLE TEST —
Protocol: Compare acid number and dissolved copper in two identical tanks—one with dosing, one without—under accelerated aging (85°C, 72 hours). Instruments: ASTM D664 titration kit for acid number, ICP-MS for copper. Pass/fail: Dosed tank must show ≤50% acid number rise and ≤30% dissolved copper vs. control. Duration: 72 hours. Kill criterion: If dosed tank exceeds 70% of control values, mechanism fails.
